claims.text: An integrated combination of electromagnetic levitation, ultrafast DSC, high-speed imaging, and CALPHAD can accurately and efficiently determine fusion and liquid-phase thermodynamic properties across the HEA family.
HEA specimens can be produced by conventional casting or powder-based methods.
Such specimens can have minimal contamination and a homogeneous microstructure.
A high-purity inert-gas environment or high vacuum avoids heterogeneous nucleation during these measurements.
Optimized heating and cooling rates minimize superheating and undercooling effects.
A temperature range of 1000–2000 °C is typical for refractory HEAs.
The intervention produces a homogeneous, containerless liquid phase.
The containerless liquid state prevents contamination and unwanted interfacial effects.
Electromagnetic levitation eliminates sample contact with crucibles.
Crucible contact can induce heterogeneous nucleation and contamination.
Ultrafast DSC provides high-resolution heat-flow measurements during melting.
In situ high-speed imaging can measure volume changes during melting in real time.
CALPHAD can relate measured heat flow to enthalpy, entropy, and liquid structure.
CALPHAD-assisted interpretation can reconcile experimental scatter across complex HEA composition space.
The methodology will measure melting temperatures with an accuracy of ±5 °C.
The methodology will determine enthalpy and entropy of fusion with high quantitative fidelity and volume changes with relative uncertainties of a few percent.
The method will uniformly capture fusion characteristics despite compositional complexity across the HEA family.
Conventional crucible-based DSC with slower heating rates often incurs errors from heterogeneous nucleation, contamination, and incomplete capture of rapid liquid-phase transitions.
The proposed approach is primarily applicable to HEAs that form homogeneous liquids without substantial segregation or decomposition during melting.
Severe microsegregation or sluggish phase reactions may require corrections or alternative measurement methods and may limit high-throughput efficiency.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis and predicted outcome claim family-wide, uniform applicability, whereas the boundary restricts applicability primarily to alloys that melt homogeneously without significant segregation or decomposition.

Conventional crucible-based DSC is characterized as error-prone, yet agreement with that same method is used as an independent accuracy benchmark capable of falsifying the proposed approach. Extensive calibration mitigates but does not fully resolve this benchmark-role tension.
